title: Humanoid Robot Operating System
subtitle: Lead software development for humanoid robot
short_description: A two-wheeled autonomous robot that follows a taped track using an IR sensor array and a tuned PID control loop, holding speed through sharp corners without losing the line.

main_media.title: Final chassis, top view
main_media.caption: Custom PCB mounted above the IR sensor array and drive motors.

items.title: Bare PCB
items.caption: First revision board fresh off the mill.

items.title: Populated board
items.caption: Sensor array and motor drivers soldered in.

blocks.content: The first revision used a fixed-gain proportional controller, which oscillated badly on tight corners. Moving to a full PID loop with gain scheduling based on error magnitude let the robot hold near-top speed on straights while slowing smoothly into turns.

blocks.title: Tuning session
blocks.caption: Logging sensor error against wheel speed to hand-tune PID gains.

blocks.content: Final lap times improved by 38% over the proportional-only version, with zero track departures across 20 consecutive test laps.

title: 3-DOF Desktop Robotic Arm
subtitle: Inverse-kinematics-driven pick-and-place arm
short_description: A three-degree-of-freedom robotic arm with a custom inverse kinematics solver, designed and 3D-printed from scratch for a desktop pick-and-place demo.

main_media.title: Assembled arm
main_media.caption: Full assembly with gripper attachment at rest position.

blocks.title: CAD overview
blocks.caption: Full linkage assembly modeled before any printing began.

blocks.content: Rather than use a lookup table, I derived closed-form inverse kinematics for the 3-link planar arm so any target (x, y) within the workspace maps directly to joint angles — no iterative solving needed on the microcontroller.

blocks.title: Gripper jaw (interactive)
blocks.caption: Drag to rotate — this is the actual print file for the final jaw geometry.

blocks.content: The gripper jaw went through four print iterations to get enough compliance to grip irregular objects without a force sensor, using a living-hinge geometry at the jaw base.

blocks.title: Pick-and-place demo
blocks.caption: Arm sorting objects by color using a webcam and OpenCV.

title: Modular PCB Sensor Hub
subtitle: Stackable environmental sensor boards over I2C
short_description: A stackable sensor board system where each board adds one environmental sensor over a shared I2C bus, letting a project mix and match temperature, humidity, and air-quality sensing without redesigning the base board.

main_media.title: Three-board stack
main_media.caption: Base board with humidity and air-quality daughter boards attached.

blocks.content: Each daughter board carries a unique I2C address set by a resistor-strapped address pin, so boards can be stacked in any order and combination without firmware changes on the base.

items.title: Temperature board
items.caption: Single-sensor board, smallest form factor in the stack.

items.title: Humidity board
items.caption: Includes onboard heater trace for condensation prevention.

items.title: Air quality board
items.caption: VOC sensor with dedicated shielding to reduce PCB heat coupling.

blocks.title: Bus topology
blocks.caption: Shared I2C bus routed through the board-to-board stacking connector.
